# Music

Card type `custom:houseview-media_player-card`, or `type: media_player` in the `cards` list of `custom:houseview-card`. Available since 1.0.

A now-playing panel for a `media_player.*` entity: a large rounded album cover with the title and artist over its
lower edge, a progress bar with elapsed and remaining time, shuffle / previous / play-pause / next / repeat, a volume
button showing the current volume and an options button (hold the dots over the cover) that opens the more-info dialog.

* Previous and next are enabled when the entity advertises the `supported_features` bits 16 and 32; the volume
  keys when it advertises bit 4; shuffle and repeat with bits 32768 and 262144. Play / pause is enabled whenever the
  speaker is available.
* Play / pause sends `media_play_pause` while playing or paused. An idle player advertising PLAY (bit 512) resumes
  its queue with `media_play`. Other inactive players open more-info. On a large tile, hold the track title or
  artist to open speaker controls. On a small panel tile (about 225 × 178, when four controls share a 480 × 480
  screen), a tap or a long press on the track title opens this same player full screen first, with the cover,
  progress, shuffle, repeat and larger keys. Play, volume and Browse on the tile keep working. Close with X or
  Escape. Speaker settings are the dots, or a hold on the title once that full player is open.
* The volume button opens the [full-screen volume view](../overviews/volume.md). Drag vertically to choose 0–100%;
  release sends one `media_player.volume_set` command. Zero stays silent without stopping playback. Mute/unmute
  appears when supported. Opening the view never starts or pauses music. Shuffle calls `shuffle_set`; repeat steps
  through off, all and one with `repeat_set`.
* Drag the progress bar, or tap a point on it, to seek when the player advertises [seek support](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/media-player/) (bit 2). The elapsed and remaining times follow your finger; release sends one `media_player.media_seek` command. Arrow keys, Home and End work too. Cancelled drags and track changes send no seek. Rapid adjustments keep only the latest queued position. Live radio, line-in, unavailable players and tracks with no duration stay read-only.
* The progress bar needs `media_duration` (radio streams have none and show an empty bar). It advances once a second
  while the player is `playing`.
* Artwork is shown only when `entity_picture` points to `/api/media_player_proxy/` on this Home Assistant
  (the page origin or the configured base URL). Anything else falls back to a music-note icon.
* While a speaker plays and nobody touches the screen, the [cover art](../overviews/cover_art.md) overview can take
  the whole screen (see the `music_screensaver` card option).

On compact square-panel tiles, the volume and Browse buttons, track information and playback controls occupy separate rows. Buttons keep
at least 44-pixel touch targets at a 225 × 178 tile size, including seeking for tracks with a known duration, so four tiles can share a 480 × 480 screen with the header enabled.
Older panel browsers without container queries use a compact layout with fixed pixel sizes.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entity | entity | required | A `media_player.*` entity |
| name | string | friendly name | Read by screen readers (the panel shows the track, not the name) |
| size | normal/wide/tall/large | normal | Widget size on carousel pages |

```yaml
type: custom:houseview-media_player-card
entity: media_player.living_room
```

## Playlists and favourites

Browse appears when the speaker supports Home Assistant media browsing. It opens a teal glass library with artwork and six large tiles per page; swipe left/right or use the arrows to move through the list without scrolling. Back or Escape returns to the player. Opening, refreshing and editing this library never starts playback. Press a playlist tile to play it on that card’s speaker and return to the player after Home Assistant accepts playback. A failed request keeps the browser open with an error so you can retry. Artwork fills the width of each rounded glass tile, with its name below.

In the native card editor, set **Shown playlists** to **Selected favourites**, then choose items under **Choose and order playlists**. Drag the selected chips to set their order. Each media card saves its own selection. **All favourites** is the default; an empty selected list deliberately shows none. Saved missing items remain visible in settings and disabled in the browser until removed or restored.

Sonos playlists, radio stations and albums should first be saved in Sonos Favourites. Discovery reads Home Assistant’s standard media browser, including Sonos’s grouped favourites; it does not sign in to Spotify or Apple Music or crawl an entire library. Unsupported speakers keep their existing controls. A failed read offers Refresh and never substitutes another speaker or playlist. The library pauses idle screensavers while open.

Playlist artwork uses the thumbnail URL returned by Home Assistant’s media browser. This can be a music-provider image or a URL on your Sonos speaker; Sonos cannot proxy all favourite artwork. Image requests omit the page referrer, and HouseView never adds Home Assistant authentication to an external image URL. Missing, invalid or failed images retain the playlist icon. Artwork URLs are never saved in the dashboard.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| playlist_mode | all/selected | all, or selected when playlists is supplied | Show all discovered favourites or only chosen items |
| playlists | list of strings | [] | Ordered opaque media keys produced by the native picker; use the editor rather than hand-writing IDs |
